* macOS (my laptop)
* [UTM](https://mac.getutm.app/) to run Ubuntu Server on Mac
* Ubuntu Server 22.04 (inside UTM)
* Docker
* Pi-hole (ad-blocking DNS)
* Unbound (recursive DNS resolver)
* Tailscale (zero-config VPN)

```shell
sudo docker run -d \
  --name pihole \
  -p 53:53/tcp -p 53:53/udp \
  -p 80:80 \
  -p 443:443 \
  -e TZ="Asia/Kolkata" \
  -e WEBPASSWORD="yourpassword" \
  -v $(pwd)/pihole/etc-pihole:/etc/pihole \
  -v $(pwd)/pihole/etc-dnsmasq.d:/etc/dnsmasq.d \
  --dns=127.0.0.1 --dns=1.1.1.1 \
  --restart=unless-stopped \
  --cap-add=NET_ADMIN \
  pihole/pihole:latest
```


evidence_refs.id: readme:8. Set Global DNS in Tailscale (No Need to Configure Each Device):9ad566f8a08122caba945ec674d8c1daacb6f7de6daf36781d4438e5c7cdf82c
evidence_refs.section: 8. Set Global DNS in Tailscale (No Need to Configure Each Device)
evidence_refs.text:
Instead of changing DNS settings manually on every device, I used Tailscale’s admin panel:

1. Went to [https://login.tailscale.com](https://login.tailscale.com/)
2. Opened the **DNS** section
3. Added Pi-hole’s Tailscale IP (100.x.x.x) as **Global Nameserver**
4. Saved and synced settings

Now every Tailscale-connected device automatically uses Pi-hole for DNS. Super easy.

![dns-override](/screenshots/Tailscale-global-dns.png)

---

```shell
nslookup doubleclick.net 100.x.x.x
```

Should return:

```shell
Name: doubleclick.net
Address: 0.0.0.0
```

![remote-device](/screenshots/nslookup-remote-device.png)

---

1. Remote devices connect to Pi-hole using Tailscale
2. Pi-hole blocks ads and trackers
3. Other queries go to Unbound for secure, recursive resolution
4. Everything stays encrypted, private, and works even behind CGNAT


📝 Note: The connection from Unbound to the root DNS servers is not encrypted (DNS still uses port 53).
But the traffic from your device to Pi-hole (and Unbound) is fully encrypted through Tailscale, so your ISP or others can’t see or log your DNS activity.
Later, you can add DNS-over-HTTPS for full end-to-end encryption.


![architecture](/screenshots/Network-diagram.png)

自由上网方法 

                           一键翻墙浏览器

永久免费。不用安装，无需设置，解压后使用。稳定、流畅、高速，长期更新。

介绍：GoProxy ipv6版、GoAgent ipv6版、v2ray版、SSR版、赛风版、WuJie版、FreeGate版、SkyZip版，适合windows操作系统，比如：Xp、win7、win8、win10系统。浏览器自带翻译插件和YouTube视频下载脚本，方便且实用。压缩包文件的格式是7z，如果解压出错，用7解压软件来解压（7z解压软件下载地址）。

注意：软件都是采用加密方式的，但为了更稳定、更安全的翻墙，建议卸载国产杀毒软件，至少翻墙时不要用它们！因为很多国产杀毒软件，比如360安全卫生、360杀毒软件、腾讯管家、金山卫士等不仅仅会起干扰作用，造成软件无法正常使用或速度变慢，它们与防火墙还有千丝万缕的关系!其实win10自带的defender就有杀毒的功能，如果还需要安全软件，可以用国外的杀毒软件avast，防火墙simplewall，还有清理软件wisecare365。它们都是免费的，而且不会干扰电脑运行。

选择指南：有GoProxy ipv6版、GoAgent ipv6版、v2ray版、SSR版、赛风版、WuJie版、FreeGate版、SkyZip版,可以按照顺序依次尝试。由于国内网络环境不同、地区不同，封锁强度会不同，所以使用效果会有差别，有的地区几乎所有的软件都能使用，有的只能用几款，因此具体哪款软件适合你的网络环境，需要你自己来尝试。内存低于2G的电脑建议用火狐翻墙浏览器。还有直翻通道可供选择，电脑、手机、平板都能使用。如果想自己搭建翻墙服务器，可以学习自建ss/ssr服务器教程或自建v2ray服务器教程。

2019年1月18日公告：ipv6版国内大多数地区已失效，如果你无法使用ipv6版，请更换其它类型的软件。

How to Play

The goal of surviv.io is to be the last player standing. You only live once per game - there is no respawn!

2D PUBG

If you've played other battle royale games like PUBG, Fortnite or H1Z1, then you're already halfway there! Think of surviv.io as 2D PUBG (with slightly less desync and more chicken).

Loot and Kill

You'll begin the game with no items other than a simple backpack. Move around the map to find loot: weapons, ammo, scopes, and medical items. Eliminate other players and you can take their loot!

Red = Bad!

Players aren't the only thing that can hurt you. The deadly red zone will move in from the sides of the map and deal increasingly greater damage if you stand in it. Keep an eye on the map and stay safe.

What's New!

February 24, 2020

Curveball

The Savannah has returned with a new perk to help flush snipers out of position.

The Closer Perk throws grenades much farther, allowing you to put Snipers on the move.

February 10, 2020

Keep Your Enemies Closer

PARMA recognizes this season of togetherness and generously offers to help rivals resolve their differences. The all new Heart Cannon diffuses damage taken from your frenemies. For groups of future friends, the same effect is achieved with the all-new Heart Grenade.

If you do not trust the intentions of your new friends, eat an entire box of chocolates to counter the effect of Heart Weapons.

January 27, 2020

Dodge This

Woods Mode is back with two new weapons and things are bound to get explosive. The PKM and Hawk 12G join the Woods Map arsenal, along with increased grenade capacity.

The PKM packs a punch while balancing mobility and range. Based on the M870 with an added magazine, the Hawk 12G's ammo capacity of 5 is the same as its parent weapon, the fire delay is faster and fires a tighter spread.

January 13, 2020

Stay frosty

Winter has arrived on the Island with new features and is more dangerous than ever, including PARMA's latest item, the Flask.

Track your enemy's footprints and use the Snow Fox perk to cover up your footprints. Be sure to keep moving or take freezing damage. Flasks and the Polar Bear perk keep you from freezing. And watch out for ice. It's slippery.

December 30, 2019

Free Fryer

PARMA's FSTMS division is pleased to introduce the next generation in starch-based modern warfare: the spud gun.

Officially designated the SMG-8 (Spud Missile Generator), the spud gun uses a proprietary breech-to-muzzle heat expander to fry and propel wedge-shaped projectiles at tremendous speeds. Like its cousin, the potato cannon, the spud gun also features nitroglycerin-spiked ammunition and a nifty tuber replication device!

projects.description: This is a Behavior Tree library meant to be an alternative to SMACH, FlexBE and the like. It includes a ReactJS-based web GUI and all the building blocks you need to build moderately advanced mission control Behavior Trees without writing a single line of code! Its claim to fame is the ability to shove, or transparently remote-execute, parts of a Behavior Tree. This implementation of Behavior trees was primarily done by Nils Berg in his thesis Distributed Execution of Behavior Trees using Heterogeneous Robot Teams. It was then improved and heavily upgraded by Kai-Uwe Hermann first with his thesis On-Line task allocation in an ad-hoc network of complex robots, currently as part of his research work. These works and the capability concept are part of Georg Heppners ongoing PhD Thesis Fähigkeitsbasierte Kooperation von Heterogenen Robotersystemen.

projects.description: The aim of this assignment is to have you do TCP socket client / server programming using I/O multiplexing, child processes and threads. It also aims at getting you to familiarize yourselves with the inetd superserver daemon, the ‘exec’ family of functions, various socket error scenarios, some socket options, and some basic domain name / IP address conversion functions. Apart from the material in Chapters 1 to 6 covered in class, you will also need to refer to the following :  the exec family of functions (Section 4.7 of Chapter 4)  using pipes for interprocess communication (IPC) in Unix  error scenarios induced by process terminations & host crashes (Sections 5.11 to 5.16, Chapter 5)  setsockopt function & SO_REUSEADDR socket option (Section 7.2 & pp.210-213, Chapter 7)  gethostbyname & gethostbyaddr functions (Sections 11.3 & 11.4, Chapter 11)  the basic structure of inetd (Section 13.5, Chapter 13)  programming with threads (Sections 26.1 to 26.5, Chapter 26) Overview  I shall present an overview of this assignment and discuss some of the specification details given below in class on Wednesday, September 17 & Monday, September 22.  Client  The client is evoked with a command line argument giving either the server IP address in dotted decimal notation, or the server domain name. The client has to be able to handle either mode and figure out which of the two is being passed to it. If it is given the IP address, it calls the gethostbyaddr function to get the domain name, which it then prints out to the user in the form of an appropriate message (e.g., ‘The server host is compserv1.cs.stonybrook.edu’). The function gethostbyname, on the other hand, returns the IP address that corresponds to a given domain name. The client then enters an infinite loop in which it queries the user which service is being requested. There are two options : echo and time (note that time is a slightly modified version of the daytime service – see below). The client then forks off a child. After the child is forked off, the parent process enters a second loop in which it continually reads and prints out status messages received from the child via a half-duplex pipe (see below). The parent exits the second loop when the child closes the pipe (how does the parent detect this?), and/or the SIGCHLD signal is generated when the child terminates. The parent then repeats the outer loop, querying the user again for the (next) service s/he desires. This cycle continues till the user responds to a query with quit rather than echo or time.  The child process is the one which handles the actual service for the user. It execs (see Section 4.7, Chapter 4) an xterm to generate a separate window through which all interactions with server and user take place. For example, the following exec function call evokes an xterm, and gets the xterm to execute echocli, located in the current directory, passing the string 127.0.0.1 (assumed to be the IP address of the server) as the command line argument argv[1] to echocli (click on the url for further details) :  execlp("xterm", "xterm", "-e", "./echocli", "127.0.0.1", (char *) 0)  xterm executes one of two client programs (echocli or timecli, say) depending on the service requested. A client program establishes a TCP connection to the server at the ‘well-known port’ for the service (in reality, this port will, of course, be some ephemeral port of your choosing, the value of which is known to both server and client code). All interaction with the user, on the one hand, and with the server, on the other, takes place through the child’s xterm window, not the parent’s window. On the other hand, the child will use a half-duplex pipe to relay status information to the parent which the parent prints out in its window (see below).To terminate the echo client, the user can type in ^D (CTRL D, the EOF character). To terminate the time client, the only option is for the user to type in ^C (CTRL C). (This can also be used as an alternative means of terminating the echo client.) Note that using ^C in the context of the time service will give the server process the impression that the client process has ‘crashed’. It is your responsibility to ensure that the server process handles this correctly and closes cleanly. I shall address this further when discussing the server process.  It is also part of your responsibility in this assignment to ensure that the client code is robust with respect to the server process crashing (see Sections 5.12 & 5.13, Chapter 5). Amongst other implications, this means that it would probably be a good idea for you to implement your echo client code along the lines of either : Figure 6.9, p.168 (or even Figure 6.13, p.174) which uses I/O multiplexing with the select function; or of Figure 26.2, p.680, which uses threads; rather than along the lines of Figure 5.5, p.125.  When the child terminates, either normally or abnormally, its xterm window disappears instantaneously. Consequently, any status information that the child might want to communicate to the user should not be printed out on the child’s xterm window, since the user will not have time to see the final such message before the window disappears. Instead, as the parent forks off the child at the beginning, a half-duplex pipe should be established from child to parent. The child uses the pipe to send status reports to the parent, which the parent prints out in its window. I leave it up to you to decide what status information exactly should be relayed to the parent but, at a minimum, the parent should certainly be notified, in as precise terms as possible, of any abnormal termination conditions of the service provided by the child.  In general, you should try to make your code as robust as possible with respect to handling errors, including confused behaviour by the user (e.g., passing an invalid command line argument; responding to a query incorrectly; trying to interact with the service through the parent process window, not the child process xterm; etc.). Amongst other things, you have to worry about EINTR errors occurring during slow system calls (such as the parent reading from the pipe, or, possibly, printing to stdout, for example) due to a SIGCHLD signal. What about other kinds of errors? Which ones can occur? How should you handle them?  Server  The server has to be able to handle multiple clients using threads (specifically, detached threads), not child processes (see Sections 26.1 to 26.4, Chapter 26). Furthermore, it has to be able to handle multiple types of service; in our case, two : echo and time. echo is just the standard echo service we have seen in class. time is a slightly modified version of the daytime service (see Figure 1.9, p.14) : instead of sending the client the ‘daytime’ just once and closing, the service sits in an infinite loop, sending the ‘daytime’, sleeping for 5 seconds, and repeating, ad infinitum.  The server is loosely based on the way the inetd daemon works : see Figure 13.7, p.374. However, note that the differences between inetd and our server are probably more significant than the similarities: inetd forks off children, whereas our server uses threads; inetd child processes issue exec commands, which our server threads do not; etc. So you should treat Figure 13.7 (and Section 13.5, Chapter 13, generally) as a source of ideas, not as a set of specifications which you must slavishly adhere to and copy. Note, by the way, that there are some similarities between our client and inetd (primarily, forking off children which issue execs), which could be a useful source of ideas.  The server creates a listening socket for each type of service that it handles, bound to the ‘well-known port’ for that service. It then uses select to await clients (Chapter 6; or, if you prefer, poll; note that pselect is not supported in Solaris 2.10). The socket on which a client connects identifies the service the client is seeking. The server accepts the connection and creates a thread which provides the service. The thread detaches itself. Meanwhile, the main thread goes back to the select to await further clients.  A major concern when using threads is to make sure that operations are thread safe (see p.685 and on into Section 26.5). In this respect, Stevens’ readline function (in Stevens’ file unpv13e/lib/readline.c, see Figure 3.18, pp.91-92) poses a particular problem. On p.686, the authors give three options for dealing with this. The third option is too inefficient and should be discarded. You can implement the second option if you wish. Easiest of all would be the first option, since it involves using a thread-safe version of readline (see Figures 26.11 & 26.12) provided in file unpv13e/threads/readline.c. Whatever you do, remember that Stevens’ library, libunp.a, contains the non-thread-safe version of Figure 3.18, and that is the version that will be link-loaded to your code unless you undertake explicit steps to ensure this does not happen (libunp.a also contains the ‘wrapper’ function Readline, whose code is also in file unpv13e/lib/readline.c). Remaking your copy of libunp.a with the ‘correct’ version of readline is not a viable option because when you hand in your code, it will be compiled and link-loaded with respect to the version of libunp.a in the course account, ~cse533/Stevens/unpv13e_solaris2.10 (I do not intend to change that version since it risks creating confusion later on in the course). Also, you will probably want to use the original version of readline in the client code anyway. I am providing you with a sample Makefile which picks up the thread-safe version of readline from directory ~cse533/Stevens/unpv13e_solaris2.10/threads and uses it when making the executable for the server, but leaves the other executables it makes to link-load the non-thread-safe version from libunp.a.  Again, it is part of your responsibility to make sure that your server code is as robust as possible with respect to errors, and that the server threads terminate cleanly under all circumstances. Recall, first of all, that the client user will often use ^C (CTRL C) in the xterm to terminate the service. This will appear to the server thread as if the client process has crashed. You need to think about the error conditions that will be induced (see Sections 5.11 to 5.13, Chapter 5), and how the echo and time server code is to detect and handle these conditions. For example, the time server will almost certainly experience an EPIPE error (see Section 5.13). How should the associated SIGPIPE signal be handled? Be aware that when we return out of the Stevens’ writen function with -1 (indicating an error) and check errno, errno is sometimes equal to 0, not EPIPE (value 32). This can happen under Solaris 2.10, but I am not sure under precisely what conditions nor why. Nor am I sure if it also happens under other Unix versions, or if it also happens when using write rather than writen. The point is, you cannot depend on errno to find out what has happened to the write or writen functions. My suggestion, therefore, is that the time server should use the select function. On the one hand, select’s timeout mechanism can be used to make the server sleep for the 5 seconds. On the other hand, select should also monitor the connection socket read event because, when the client xterm is ^C’ed, a FIN will be sent to the server TCP, which will prime the socket for reading; a read on the socket will then return with value 0 (see Figure 14.3, p. 385 as an example).  But what about errors other than EPIPE? Which ones can occur? How should you handle them? Recall, as well, that if a thread terminates without explicitly closing the connection socket it has been using, the connection socket will remain existent until the server process itself dies (why?). Since the server process is supposed, in principle, to run for ever, you risk ending up with an ever increasing number of unused, ‘orphaned’ sockets unless you are careful.  Whenever a server thread detects the termination of its client, it should print out a message giving appropriate details: e.g., “Client termination: EPIPE error detected”, “Client termination: socket read returned with value 0”, “Client termination: socket read returned with value -1, errno = . . .”, and so on.  When debugging your server code, you will probably find that restarting the server very shortly after it was last running will give you trouble when it comes to bind to its ‘well-known ports’. This is because, when the server side initiates connection termination (which is what will happen if the server process crashes; or if you kill it first, before killing the client) TCP keeps the connections open in the TIME_WAIT state for 2MSLs (Sections 2.6 & 2.7, Chapter 2). This could very quickly become a major irritant. I suggest you explore the possibility of using the SO_REUSEADDR socket option (pp.210-213, Chapter 7; note that the SO_REUSEPORT socket option is not supported in Solaris 2.10), which should help keep the stress level down. You will need to use the setsockopt function (Section 7.2) to enable this option. Figure 8.24, p.263, shows an instance of server code that sets the SO_REUSEADDR socket option.  Finally, you should be aware of the sort of problem, described in Section 16.6, pp.461-463, that might occur when (blocking) listening sockets are monitored using select. Such sockets should be made nonblocking, which requires use of the fcntl  function after socket creates the socket, but before listen turns the socket into a listening socket.

evidence_refs.text:
靈犀注音 0C

免選字，把話打完。
在你的電腦上用 Transformer 看前文選字的注音輸入法，支援 Linux、macOS 與 Windows。

官網 · 下載 · 選字技術 · 操作指南 · 回報問題

> **English** — 0C (靈犀注音) is a Zhuyin (Bopomofo) input method for Traditional Chinese. An on-device Transformer language model reads what you have just written and picks the right homophones, so you can type a whole sentence without stopping to choose characters. It runs entirely on your computer, and ships shells for Fcitx5, IBus, macOS InputMethodKit and Windows TSF. ## ✨ 特色 - 🧠 **Transformer 選字**：自行訓練的語言模型參考整段前文與注音判斷同音字，大多數時候不必停下來挑字。 - ⇥ **Tab 補全**：有把握才提示後續字詞，按 Tab 接受；補全只來自詞庫與個人片語，不生成新內容。 - 🔒 **全在本機**：選字、補標點與個人學習都在你的電腦上以 CPU 執行，不連網、不上傳打字內容。 - 📚 **我的詞彙**：人名、術語、英文指令加進來就排在前面，也看得到靈犀學到了什麼。 - 🔤 **中英混打、模糊音、Emoji 與顏文字**：ㄗ／ㄓ、ㄘ／ㄔ、ㄙ／ㄕ、ㄣ／ㄥ 近音放在後面備選；按 = 開 Emoji 選單。 - 🔁 **輸出簡體字、自訂選字鍵**：看繁體打字、送出時才轉簡體，可從輸入法選單一鍵切換；選字鍵可用 1–0 或 asdfghjkl;。 - ✍️ **送出時補標點**（Beta）：Enter 送出時在漢字之間補上 ，。？！、；，不改動你打的字。 - 🛟 **自動退回**：模型無法啟動或回應太慢時改用統計引擎排序，打字不會卡住。

## 🎯 免選字是怎麼做到的 傳統注音輸入法靠詞庫與詞頻挑字，只看得到相鄰的一兩個詞。靈犀注音在統計引擎之上多了一層 Transformer 重排： ```mermaid flowchart TD K["⌨️ 注音按鍵"] --> L["📖 詞庫查詞，建立詞圖"] L --> V["📊 統計引擎：unigram／bigram＋Viterbi
取 N-best 前 8 名"] C["📝 已送出的前文
最多 64 字"] -.-> T V --> T{"🧠 Transformer 重排
前文＋注音＋候選"} T -->|"100 ms 內完成"| P["👤 套用個人詞庫"] T -.->|"逾時或模型無法使用"| F["🛟 統計排序"] F --> P P --> O["✅ 首選上屏"] O -->|"Enter 送出"| Q["✍️ 補標點（Beta）"] ``` 1. **列出可能的句子** 📖：依注音在詞庫找出所有可能的字詞，以 unigram／bigram 統計語言模型與 Viterbi 在詞圖上搜尋最可能的組合，打字時即時更新。 2. **Transformer 重排** 🧠：讀入剛送出、游標仍緊接其後的前文（最多 64 字）、目前的注音與每個候選，替前 8 名重新評分。attention 能同時參考整段前文，不只看緊鄰的詞。 3. **本機學習** 👤：你選過、改過的字詞記在本機個人詞庫，下次同樣的情況優先出現。 4. **有把握才補全** ⇥：後續字詞的信心夠高時才顯示 Tab 建議。 ## 📈 評測：首選錯誤少約六成 在事前凍結、模型沒看過的台灣新聞測試（2026-09-24〜26，共 6,000 例，一半是困難的同音短詞）上： | 方法 | 首選正確率 | 首選錯誤率 | |---|---:|---:| | 新酷音 0.11.0 | 64.2% | 35.8% | | 小麥注音 | 67.2% | 32.8% | | 靈犀注音（只用統計引擎） | 76.9% | 23.1% | | **靈犀注音（Transformer 重排）** | **86.0%／86.1%** | **14.0%** | ```mermaid xychart-beta title "首選錯誤率（越低越好）" x-axis ["新酷音", "小麥注音", "靈犀・統計", "靈犀・Transformer"] y-axis "錯誤率 %" 0 --> 40 bar [35.8, 32.8, 23.1, 14.0] ``` 測試規格、成功標準與評分程式都在讀取資料前凍結，只評一次；讀音由字典合成、答案取原文，不是真人打字紀錄。外部輸入法採對它們最有利的輸入方式、無個人詞庫。靈犀注音的兩個數字來自兩個不同的訓練種子；「只用統計引擎」也是模型無法啟動時的表現。免選字是目標而非保證：罕見人名與詞庫外的詞仍可能要手動選。 ### 🧩 模型 | | 選字（`models/select/`） | 補標點（`models/punct/`） | |---|---|---| | 架構 | 因果 Transformer decoder：8 層、寬度 512、8 個 attention head，約 3,261 萬參數 | 雙向 Transformer encoder | | 輸入 | 前文（最多 64 字）＋注音＋候選 | 送出的文字，不看前文 | | 權重 | [Funmula/0c-sequence-d512](https://huggingface.co/Funmula/0c-sequence-d512) | [Funmula/0c-punct-d512](https://huggingface.co/Funmula/0c-punct-d512) | 模型從零開始訓練，不使用通用大型語言模型的權重，採用 RoPE、GeGLU 等現代化元件。一般桌機 CPU 上選字的 P95 延遲約 7 ms（短片段）至 16 ms（長片段）；兩個模型合計約 250 MB。密碼欄位、暫停學習及英數模式下不送任何文字給模型。更多數字與方法見 [選字技術](https://0c.biggo.com/technology/)。 ## 📥 安裝 Windows、macOS、Linux 安裝包請到官網下載：👉 [0c.biggo.com/download](https://0c.biggo.com/download/) 發行版打包請用 [Releases](https://github.com/0c-biggo/0c-ime/releases/latest) 的 `0c-ime-<版本>.tar.xz`：內附現成字典，符合 DFSG，解壓即可建置；已配對的神經模型在另附的 `0c-ime-models-<版本>.tar.xz`。見 [打包與發佈](PACKAGING.md)。 ## 🛠️ 從原始碼建置 需要 Go 1.26 以上；測試與發佈工具使用 Python 3.11 以上。以下指令在 repo 根目錄執行，不會安裝或重啟桌面輸入法： ```sh git clone https://github.com/0c-biggo/0c-ime.git cd 0c-ime make assets # 下載與這份原始碼相符的字典與模型 go test ./... go run ./cmd/0c-cli -data assets/data ``` `make assets` 從同版本的 [Release](https://github.com/0c-biggo/0c-ime/releases) 取得原始碼與模型 tarball（合計約 275 MB），驗證後把現成字典放到 `assets/data/`、已配對模型放到 `models/select/` 與 `models/punct/`，和出貨內容相同；0.2.2 起 Release 附的 Source code 壓縮檔也適用。要指定版本用 `make assets RELEASE=v0.2.2`，只取字典用 `make assets MODELS=0`（約 36 MB，以統計選字運作）。 各平台外殼另需各自的工具鏈與系統函式庫： | 平台 | 外殼 | 建置說明 | |---|---|---| | 🐧 Linux | Fcitx5（C++） | [platforms/linux-fcitx5](platforms/linux-fcitx5/README.md) | | 🐧 Linux | IBus（Go） | [platforms/linux-ibus](platforms/linux-ibus/README.md) | | 🍎 macOS | InputMethodKit（Swift） | [platforms/macos](platforms/macos/README.md) | | 🪟 Windows | TSF（Rust） | [platforms/windows](platforms/windows/README.md) | | ⚙️ 設定程式 | Tauri | [platforms/settings](platforms/settings/README.md) | | 🧠 神經推論 | Python＋ONNX Runtime | [platforms/neural](platforms/neural/README.md) | ## 🗂️ 專案結構 ```text core/ 輸入法邏輯：注音解析、詞圖解碼、語言模型、候選重排、個人學習（不做 I/O） bridge/ 引擎與外殼之間的行程間通訊（IPC） internal/ 設定、自動更新、神經推論 worker、詞庫編譯與評測等共用程式 cmd/ 執行檔入口：0c-server、0c-ibus、0c-update、0c-cli、0c-compile、0c-eval… platforms/ Linux／macOS／Windows 外殼、設定程式、神經推論 data/ 詞庫來源、來源帳本與授權聲明 models/ 上游模型與字典配對的固定清單 scripts/ 建置、打包與回歸測試工具 testdata/ 測試資料 ``` 詞庫格式與資料來源見 [data/README.md](data/README.md)，模型版本與配對見 [models/README.md](models/README.md)。 ## 🤝 參與貢獻 歡迎回報問題與送 PR！請先看 [參與開發](CONTRIBUTING.md)：回報時附上版本、平台與逐鍵重現步驟；改程式前後跑一次檢查： ```sh python3 scripts/check_public_tree.py go test ./... go vet ./... make -C platforms/linux-fcitx5 test make test-upgrade make test-release ``` 版本變更見 [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)。 ## 📄 授權 自有程式採 AGPL-3.0-only，另可洽談商業授權；自有圖示與圖片採 CC BY-SA 4.0；資料、模型與第三方元件依各自授權，見 [授權說明](legal/README.md)。

evidence_refs.section: 📈 評測：首選錯誤少約六成
evidence_refs.text:
在事前凍結、模型沒看過的台灣新聞測試（2026-09-24〜26，共 6,000 例，一半是困難的同音短詞）上：

| 方法 | 首選正確率 | 首選錯誤率 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 新酷音 0.11.0 | 64.2% | 35.8% |
| 小麥注音 | 67.2% | 32.8% |
| 靈犀注音（只用統計引擎） | 76.9% | 23.1% |
| **靈犀注音（Transformer 重排）** | **86.0%／86.1%** | **14.0%** |

```mermaid
xychart-beta
    title "首選錯誤率（越低越好）"
    x-axis ["新酷音", "小麥注音", "靈犀・統計", "靈犀・Transformer"]
    y-axis "錯誤率 %" 0 --> 40
    bar [35.8, 32.8, 23.1, 14.0]
```

測試規格、成功標準與評分程式都在讀取資料前凍結，只評一次；讀音由字典合成、答案取原文，不是真人打字紀錄。外部輸入法採對它們最有利的輸入方式、無個人詞庫。靈犀注音的兩個數字來自兩個不同的訓練種子；「只用統計引擎」也是模型無法啟動時的表現。免選字是目標而非保證：罕見人名與詞庫外的詞仍可能要手動選。

| | 選字（`models/select/`） | 補標點（`models/punct/`） |
|---|---|---|
| 架構 | 因果 Transformer decoder：8 層、寬度 512、8 個 attention head，約 3,261 萬參數 | 雙向 Transformer encoder |
| 輸入 | 前文（最多 64 字）＋注音＋候選 | 送出的文字，不看前文 |
| 權重 | [Funmula/0c-sequence-d512](https://huggingface.co/Funmula/0c-sequence-d512) | [Funmula/0c-punct-d512](https://huggingface.co/Funmula/0c-punct-d512) |

模型從零開始訓練，不使用通用大型語言模型的權重，採用 RoPE、GeGLU 等現代化元件。一般桌機 CPU 上選字的 P95 延遲約 7 ms（短片段）至 16 ms（長片段）；兩個模型合計約 250 MB。密碼欄位、暫停學習及英數模式下不送任何文字給模型。更多數字與方法見 [選字技術](https://0c.biggo.com/technology/)。

Windows、macOS、Linux 安裝包請到官網下載：👉 [0c.biggo.com/download](https://0c.biggo.com/download/)

發行版打包請用 [Releases](https://github.com/0c-biggo/0c-ime/releases/latest) 的 `0c-ime-<版本>.tar.xz`：內附現成字典，符合 DFSG，解壓即可建置；已配對的神經模型在另附的 `0c-ime-models-<版本>.tar.xz`。見 [打包與發佈](PACKAGING.md)。

需要 Go 1.26 以上；測試與發佈工具使用 Python 3.11 以上。以下指令在 repo 根目錄執行，不會安裝或重啟桌面輸入法：

```sh
git clone https://github.com/0c-biggo/0c-ime.git
cd 0c-ime
make assets          # 下載與這份原始碼相符的字典與模型
go test ./...
go run ./cmd/0c-cli -data assets/data
```

`make assets` 從同版本的 [Release](https://github.com/0c-biggo/0c-ime/releases) 取得原始碼與模型 tarball（合計約 275 MB），驗證後把現成字典放到 `assets/data/`、已配對模型放到 `models/select/` 與 `models/punct/`，和出貨內容相同；0.2.2 起 Release 附的 Source code 壓縮檔也適用。要指定版本用 `make assets RELEASE=v0.2.2`，只取字典用 `make assets MODELS=0`（約 36 MB，以統計選字運作）。

各平台外殼另需各自的工具鏈與系統函式庫：

| 平台 | 外殼 | 建置說明 |
|---|---|---|
| 🐧 Linux | Fcitx5（C++） | [platforms/linux-fcitx5](platforms/linux-fcitx5/README.md) |
| 🐧 Linux | IBus（Go） | [platforms/linux-ibus](platforms/linux-ibus/README.md) |
| 🍎 macOS | InputMethodKit（Swift） | [platforms/macos](platforms/macos/README.md) |
| 🪟 Windows | TSF（Rust） | [platforms/windows](platforms/windows/README.md) |
| ⚙️ 設定程式 | Tauri | [platforms/settings](platforms/settings/README.md) |
| 🧠 神經推論 | Python＋ONNX Runtime | [platforms/neural](platforms/neural/README.md) |

```text
core/         輸入法邏輯：注音解析、詞圖解碼、語言模型、候選重排、個人學習（不做 I/O）
bridge/       引擎與外殼之間的行程間通訊（IPC）
internal/     設定、自動更新、神經推論 worker、詞庫編譯與評測等共用程式
cmd/          執行檔入口：0c-server、0c-ibus、0c-update、0c-cli、0c-compile、0c-eval…
platforms/    Linux／macOS／Windows 外殼、設定程式、神經推論
data/         詞庫來源、來源帳本與授權聲明
models/       上游模型與字典配對的固定清單
scripts/      建置、打包與回歸測試工具
testdata/     測試資料
```

詞庫格式與資料來源見 [data/README.md](data/README.md)，模型版本與配對見 [models/README.md](models/README.md)。

歡迎回報問題與送 PR！請先看 [參與開發](CONTRIBUTING.md)：回報時附上版本、平台與逐鍵重現步驟；改程式前後跑一次檢查：

```sh
python3 scripts/check_public_tree.py
go test ./...
go vet ./...
make -C platforms/linux-fcitx5 test
make test-upgrade
make test-release
```


projects.name: MacShell
projects.description: MacOS Tahoe-like shell for Hyprland

evidence_refs.text:
MacShell

A macOS Tahoe–style menu bar + Dock for Hyprland, built on Quickshell,
with a real-time Liquid Glass refraction shader, and a lock screen, MacLock.


Quick showcase (OLD)

Screenshots · Requirements · Install · Updating · Hyprland config · MacLock · Troubleshooting

--- A macOS Tahoe–style **menu bar + Dock** for Hyprland, built on [Quickshell](https://quickshell.org), with a real-time "Liquid Glass" refraction shader, window previews, Spotlight, clipboard/emoji picker, notifications, Control Center, screenshots, screen recording, desktop widgets (weather, calendar, clock, music player), a wallpaper picker, an Alt+Tab switcher and a full lock screen, all in one Quickshell process. The repository also ships **MacLock**, a matching Liquid Glass lock screen. It is a separate Quickshell config on purpose: it runs as its own process, so a shell crash can never take the lock with it. Best icon pack for the shell: https://github.com/Scrimas/MacOS-Like > **Heads up:** this targets **Hyprland 0.55+ with a Lua config** (`hyprland.lua`) and a recent **Quickshell (0.3.x)**. > See [Requirements](#requirements) and [Known issues](#known-issues). ## Screenshots ### MacShell **The whole desktop:** widgets, the menu bar on top and the Dock at the bottom.

**The Dock,** with Liquid Glass.

**Control Center**

### MacLock

Lock screen
Lock screen media player
## Files ``` MacShell/ (this repository) ├── install.sh installer / updater ├── README.md ├── MacShell/ the shell -> ~/.config/quickshell/MacShell └── MacLock/ the lock screen -> ~/.config/quickshell/MacLock ``` The two are installed as **separate** Quickshell configs (neither lives inside the other). **MacShell** | File | Purpose | |---|---| | `shell.qml` | Entry point. Shared hub: window geometry, wallpaper lookup, capture gating. | | `MacBar.qml` | Menu bar, Control Center, Spotlight, notifications, switcher, screenshots, wallpaper picker. | | `MacDock.qml` | Dock, window previews, and the Settings window. | | `ClockApp.qml` | The Clock app window (opened from the menu bar clock). | | `MacWidgets.qml` | Desktop widgets layer (data, placement, editing). | | `WidgetVisual.qml` | Draws one widget; shared by the desktop layer and the Liquid Glass backdrop, so menus refract the widgets too. | | `WeatherWidget.qml`, `WeatherIcon.qml`, `WeatherHourCol.qml`, `CalendarWidget.qml`, `ClockWidget.qml`, `PlayerWidget.qml`, `PlayerArt.qml`, `PlayerBtn.qml`, `PlayerGlyph.qml`, `ImageWidget.qml`, `MarqueeText.qml` | The widgets and their helpers (`ImageWidget.qml` shows a picture of your choice). | | `SPopUp.qml`, `Dissolve.qml`, `MorphText.qml`, `MorphGlyph.qml`, `WGlyph.qml`, `ClockGlyph.qml`, `Wheel.qml` | Shared UI pieces and effects. | | `liquidglass.frag` (+ `contourglow`, `tintcard`, `dust`, `burn`, `fade`) | Shaders. Prebuilt `.frag.qsb` files ship next to them; `liquidglass.frag` is recompiled with `qsb` on first run. | | `EmojiData.js` | Emoji fallback data for Spotlight (from [gemoji](https://github.com/github/gemoji), MIT). | | `macshell-update` | Update tool (installed to `~/.local/bin`, see [Updating](#updating)). The installer also writes `macshell-start`, the script the Hyprland autostart runs. | | `apple-logo-black.svg`, `apple-logo-white.svg` | Menu bar logo. | | `assets/` | Icons and the credits pictures. | **MacLock** | File | Purpose | |---|---| | `shell.qml` | Entry point: session lock, IPC (`lockscreen`), preview mode. | | `LockScreen.qml` | The lock screen UI and PAM password check. | | `lock-via-ipc.sh` | Helper for your keybind: starts MacLock if needed, then locks. | | `Glass.qml`, `Glyph.qml`, `MorphGlyph.qml`, `MorphText.qml`, `ClockGlyph.qml`, `ContourGlow.qml` and the `*.frag` / `*.qsb` shaders | Visuals. | | `hyprland.lua` | Snippet with the keybind (copy it into your config). | and more files... ## Requirements ### Required | What | Why | |---|---| | **Hyprland ≥ 0.55, running a Lua config** (`~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`) | Window actions, the Alt+Tab focus, "paste after picking", Log Out and the floating Settings window use Lua dispatches (`hyprctl dispatch 'hl.dsp…'`, `hyprctl eval`). On older versions or a `.conf` session these actions fail; the bar, Dock, glass and previews still work. Quick test: `hyprctl dispatch 'hl.dsp.no_op()'` must not error. | | **Quickshell ≥ 0.3.0** (0.3.2 recommended) | Needs the Hyprland module (`HyprlandToplevel`, `lastIpcObject`, Lua-config support), `ScreencopyView`, `IpcHandler`, and the UPower / Pipewire / Mpris / SystemTray / Notifications services. | | Quickshell built with **Wayland**, **Hyprland**, **Screencopy → Hyprland Toplevel Export**, **Pipewire**, **UPower**, **Mpris**, **System Tray** | Distro packages normally enable all of these. Check the build info that `qs` prints in its logs. | | **Qt 6.5+** with `qt6-declarative`, `qt6-wayland`, **`qt6-shadertools`** (provides `qsb`) | `QtQuick.Effects` (MultiEffect) needs 6.5+. `qsb` compiles `liquidglass.frag` on first run. Without it (and without a prebuilt `liquidglass.frag.qsb`) the glass falls back to "Normal Blur". | | `qt6-svg` (recommended) | SVG app icons. | | `hyprctl`, `sh`, `xdg-open` | Core. | | An **icon theme** (Papirus, Adwaita, …) set for Qt apps | App icons in the Dock and Spotlight come from the system theme. If icons are blank, set one with `qt6ct` or `QS_ICON_THEME`. | | `curl`, `tar` | Used by the installer and the updater, and by the Weather widget. | | Font **Inter** (default) | Falls back to the system font; "Noto Sans" / "System" can be chosen in Settings. | ### MacLock (only if you use the lock screen) | What | Why | |---|---| | A PAM stack at `/etc/pam.d/hyprlock` (installed by the `hyprlock` package) | MacLock checks passwords with it. The installer warns if the file is missing. | | Quickshell with the **Pam** and **session-lock** modules | Distro packages normally include them. | | Hyprland `misc:allow_session_lock_restore` (recommended) | Lets a restarted MacLock take over a lock if it ever dies. | ### Optional (missing tools just disable that feature) | Feature | Tool(s) | |---|---| | Screenshots (Print key) | `grim`, `wl-clipboard` (clipboard copy), `libnotify` (`notify-send`) | | Clipboard history + Emoji (Spotlight) | `wl-clipboard`, `cliphist` (the shell starts the `wl-paste --watch cliphist store` watchers itself) | | Screen recording | `wf-recorder` | | Color picker | `hyprpicker` | | Night Shift | `hyprsunset` | | Brightness | `brightnessctl` | | Wi-Fi / VPN / Ethernet | NetworkManager (`nmcli`); fallback editor `nm-connection-editor` or `nmtui` | | Bluetooth | `bluez` (`bluetoothctl`) **and the `bluetooth` service running** (`sudo systemctl enable --now bluetooth`; the installer offers to do this), `rfkill` (util-linux) to un-block the adapter | | Audio device routing | `wpctl` (WirePlumber) or `pactl` | | Privacy indicators | PipeWire (`pw-dump`) | | Keep Awake | `systemd-inhibit` | | Lock / Sleep / Restart / Shut Down | `loginctl`, `systemctl` (UWSM sessions are stopped via `uwsm`) | | Trash watching / emptying | `inotify-tools` (`inotifywait`), `ktrash6`/`ktrash5`, or a file manager (`dolphin`, `nautilus`, `thunar`, `nemo`, `pcmanfm-qt`) | | Folder pickers in Settings, picking a picture for an Image widget | `zenity`, `kdialog` or `yad` | | "About This Linux" | `fastfetch` or `neofetch` | | Do Not Disturb (Focus) | `dunstctl`, `makoctl` or `swaync-client` (only if you keep one of those) | | Emoji search keywords | `emoji-test.txt` from the `unicode-emoji` package (otherwise `EmojiData.js` is used) | | Setting the wallpaper | `awww` (recommended; its daemon is started for you). Fallbacks: `swww`, Noctalia, `hyprpaper`, `swaybg` — or set a command yourself (see [Wallpaper](#wallpaper)) | | Animated (video) wallpapers | `mpvpaper`, `ffmpeg` (thumbnails and previews) | | Installer extras | `rsync` (faster file sync), `systemd` (daily automatic updates) | | Default apps | terminal `kitty`, file opener `xdg-open` — change `terminal`, `launcher`, `filesCmd`, `clipboardCmd` in `~/.config/macbar/settings.json` | ### Conflicts This shell **replaces** your bar, dock and notification daemon. Stop anything that overlaps: - Other bars/shells (waybar, hyprpanel, ags, Noctalia, Caelestia, …) and docks (nwg-dock, …). - Notification daemons (`dunst`, `mako`, `swaync`): the bar owns `org.freedesktop.Notifications`. `systemctl --user disable --now dunst` (or `mako` / `swaync`). ## Install 1. Install the requirements above. On Arch, for example: ```sh sudo pacman -Syu sudo pacman -S --needed \ hyprland quickshell hyprlock awww \ qt6-base qt6-declarative qt6-wayland qt6-shadertools qt6-svg \ grim slurp wl-clipboard wf-recorder cliphist \ libnotify brightnessctl \ networkmanager bluez bluez-utils \ inotify-tools \ inter-font noto-fonts noto-fonts-emoji \ xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland \ xdg-utils polkit \ pipewire wireplumber pipewire-pulse \ kitty ``` Other distros: install the equivalents. Fedora has a Quickshell COPR; Nix has `pkgs.quickshell`. You can skip this: the installer checks every requirement (tools, Qt libraries, fonts, icon theme, portals, `hyprlock`, the optional helpers such as `awww`, `zenity`, `slurp`, `ffmpeg`) and installs the missing ones for you with pacman, dnf or apt, after asking once (`-y` skips the question). Packages that are not in the main repositories, such as `quickshell` or `awww`, come from the AUR (`yay` / `paru`; on Arch the installer can build `yay` for you) or the Fedora COPR. It also enables the `bluetooth` service, which Bluetooth needs. `bash install.sh --deps-only` does just this step. Hyprland 0.55+ with a Lua config may need a newer package than your distro ships, so check `hyprctl version`. Debian/Ubuntu have no `quickshell` / `hyprland` packages: build those from source. 2. Run the installer, either from a clone: ```sh git clone https://github.com/0-ss/MacShell cd MacShell bash install.sh ``` or in one line: ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0-ss/MacShell/main/install.sh | bash ``` It installs **MacShell** to `~/.config/quickshell/MacShell` and **MacLock** to `~/.config/quickshell/MacLock`, and adds the autostart to your Hyprland config: a block in `hyprland.lua` (Hyprland 0.55+), or an `exec-once` line in `hyprland.conf` when there is no Lua config. The block runs `~/.local/bin/macshell-start`, which waits for the compositor, never starts a second copy and restarts the shell if it crashes. Remove the block between the `MacShell (added by install.sh)` markers to undo it. Your settings are never touched, and the previous install is backed up first (last 3 kept in `~/.local/share/macshell/backups/`). When run from a clone, the installer first checks GitHub: if the repository has a newer version (and your clone has no uncommitted changes) it downloads and installs that one automatically. Don't reach the install folders through a symlink; Quickshell ≥ 0.3 derives its state folders from the link path. 3. Try it: ```sh qs -c MacShell ``` On first run with the Liquid Glass style, `liquidglass.frag` is compiled with `qsb` and cached in `~/.config/macdock/liquidglass.frag.qsb`. Watch for `[macbar-glass] state: ready` in the log. 4. Add the Hyprland config below, then autostart it. ### Installer options | Option | Effect | |---|---| | `-y`, `--yes` | Don't ask questions (answer yes). | | `--no-deps` | Skip the dependency check and package installation. | | `--deps-only` | Only check / install dependencies (and enable the services below), then stop. | | `--doctor` | Check the whole setup (environment, services, wallpaper, shaders, Hyprland, GPU) and explain each problem. | | `--low-power` | Settings for older computers: no live window capture, no magnification, plain blur, no real-time glass. | | `--no-services` | Don't enable system services (bluetooth, NetworkManager, power-profiles-daemon, PipeWire). | | `--no-autostart` | Don't touch the Hyprland config. | | `--no-rules` | Don't add the Liquid Glass layer rules to the Hyprland config. | | `--channel release\|main` | `release` (default): latest release, or the newest commit if there are none. `main`: always the newest commit. | | `--no-lock` | Install MacShell only, without MacLock. | | `--check` | Only check for a newer version (exit 0 = up to date, 10 = update available). | | `--local` | Install the local clone as it is, don't look for a newer version on GitHub. | | `--auto-update` / `--no-auto-update` | Set up / remove a daily systemd user timer that installs updates by itself. | | `--ref REF` | Install a specific tag or commit. | | `--from-dir DIR` | Install from a local folder instead of downloading. | | `--uninstall` | Remove MacShell and MacLock (settings are kept). | Environment: `MACSHELL_REPO`, `MACSHELL_BRANCH`, `MACSHELL_CHANNEL`, `MACSHELL_DEST`, `MACLOCK_DEST`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`. ## Updating The Best way to make sure you have the latest update Is to delete the MacShell folder in /home (IF needed) and run this again : ```sh git clone https://github.com/0-ss/MacShell cd MacShell bash install.sh ``` or you can use this method : Run the installer (`./install.sh` in your clone, or `macshell-install` from anywhere). It shows a menu: ``` MacShell (installed: a1b2c3d4e5f6) 1) Install shell 2) Check for updates 3) Uninstall shell 4) Bind help q) Quit ``` - **Install shell** installs MacShell and MacLock (or reinstalls them). - **Check for updates** compares your version with GitHub and, if there is a newer one, asks whether to install it (y/n). - **Uninstall shell** removes MacShell and MacLock (your settings are kept). - **Bind help** opens the Hyprland keybind section of this README in your browser. The other tools are still available as options: `--doctor`, `--low-power`, `--deps-only` (see `--help`). An update also installs the dependencies the new version needs, updates MacShell and MacLock together, saves the old install first, and never touches your settings. The command-line tool is still there for scripts and the daily timer: ```sh macshell-update check # is there a newer version? macshell-update log # what changed since the installed version macshell-update update # download and install it (MacShell and MacLock), including new dependencies macshell-update rollback # go back to the previous install (MacShell and MacLock) macshell-update channel main # follow the newest commit instead of releases (or: release) macshell-update status ``` `macshell-update update` runs the *new* version's installer too, so new files, new dependencies and a new start script come along. It keeps the last 3 installs, and does one update at a time. Dependencies are installed only when `sudo` works without a password (an unattended timer cannot type one); otherwise you get a notice listing what to install with `bash install.sh --deps-only`. The shell also checks by itself and tells you. `bash install.sh --check` does the same check from a clone, and `bash install.sh --auto-update` installs a daily timer (`systemctl --user list-timers macshell-update.timer`) so updates install without you doing anything. MacShell reloads itself after an update; MacLock picks up the new files the next time it locks. ## Hyprland configuration (Lua) ```lua -- autostart (remove other bars / docks / notification daemons first). -- install.sh adds this for you; macshell-start waits for the compositor and restarts the shell if it crashes. hl.on("hyprland.start", function() hl.exec_cmd("sh ~/.local/bin/macshell-start") end) -- layer rules: blur for the glass surfaces hl.layer_rule({ name = "macdock", match = { namespace = "macdock" }, blur = true, ignore_alpha = 0.2, no_anim = true }) hl.layer_rule({ name = "macspot", match = { namespace = "macspot" }, blur = true, ignore_alpha = 0.05, no_anim = true }) hl.layer_rule({ name = "macbarbg", match = { namespace = "macbarbg" }, blur = true, ignore_alpha = 0.05, no_anim = true }) hl.layer_rule({ name = "macshot", match = { namespace = "macshot" }, no_anim = true }) -- optional: no fade on the screenshot picker -- The Settings window floats and centres itself when it opens, so it needs no window rule. -- keybinds (the name after -c is the config folder name, case-sensitive) local qs = "qs -c MacShell ipc call " hl.bind("SUPER + V", hl.dsp.exec_cmd(qs .. "spotlight clipboard")) hl.bind("SUPER + period", hl.dsp.exec_cmd(qs .. "spotlight emoji")) hl.bind("SUPER + Space", hl.dsp.exec_cmd(qs .. "spotlight toggle")) hl.bind("ALT + TAB", hl.dsp.exec_cmd(qs .. "switcher next")) hl.bind("CTRL + ALT + W", hl.dsp.exec_cmd(qs .. "wallpapers toggle")) hl.bind("PRINT", hl.dsp.exec_cmd(qs .. "screenshot region")) -- MacLock (lock screen) hl.bind("SUPER + L", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("sh ~/.config/quickshell/MacLock/lock-via-ipc.sh")) ``` Change `SUPER + L` if that key is already used. On a classic `hyprland.conf` the same bind is `bind = SUPER, L, exec, sh ~/.config/quickshell/MacLock/lock-via-ipc.sh`. Also make sure **blur is enabled** in your Hyprland `decoration` settings, or the "Normal Blur" style won't blur. ### IPC reference `qs -c MacShell ipc call ` | Target | Functions | |---|---| | `spotlight` | `toggle`, `clipboard`, `emoji`, `apps` | | `screenshot` | `region`, `screen`, `window` | | `wallpapers` | `toggle`, `open`, `close` | | `switcher` | `next`, `prev`, `commit`, `cancel` | | `settings` | `open` (works even if both the bar and the Dock are disabled) | | `widgets` | `refresh` (re-fetch the weather), `edit true\|false` (move / remove desktop widgets) | | `glass` | `captures true\|false` (window previews on/off, same as Settings → Dock Behavior → *Live window capture*) | ## MacLock A macOS-style lock screen using the same Liquid Glass look (see the [screenshots](#maclock-1) above). Each lock runs in its own process (a Wayland session lock is used once), and `lock-via-ipc.sh` starts a fresh one for every lock, so the keybind above is all you need. ```sh sh ~/.config/quickshell/MacLock/lock-via-ipc.sh # lock now (what the keybind runs) qs -c MacLock ipc call lockscreen lock # same, if an IPC-ready MacLock is already running qs -c MacLock # lock immediately, one-shot (e.g. from hypridle) MACLOCK_PREVIEW=1 qs -c MacLock # preview the design as a window, no real lock ``` Passwords are checked with PAM (`/etc/pam.d/hyprlock`). To lock on idle or before sleep with `hypridle`, set `lock_cmd = sh ~/.config/quickshell/MacLock/lock-via-ipc.sh`. ## Dock icon tint Settings → Desktop & Dock → Icon Tint re-colours every Dock icon with one colour (pick a swatch or type a hex colour) and works with any icon pack: each icon is desaturated and colourised with your colour, with a small brightness lift so light colours (green, yellow...) stay vivid and black stays dark. **Strength** keeps some of the original colours. It needs no shader build and no extra packages. ## Desktop widgets Settings → General → Desktop Widgets. Weather, Calendar, Clock, Player and **Image** widgets, each in Small, Medium and Large. **Widget size** scales every widget and the grid together (60 % to 150 %); widgets snap back onto the grid when you let go of the slider. An Image widget shows a picture you choose: press **+ S / M / L** on the Image row and pick a file (needs `zenity`, `kdialog` or `yad`). The picture is copied to `~/.config/macwidgets/images`, so it keeps working if the original moves. To change it later use **Edit on Desktop** and press **Choose Image…** on the widget. ## Wallpaper Changing the wallpaper from Settings, the wallpaper picker (Ctrl+Alt+W) or `ipc call wallpapers` sets the real desktop wallpaper with **`awww`** (its daemon is started automatically if needed), and the widgets, menus and Liquid Glass follow. Light/Dark wallpaper pairs (`name-Light.png` / `name-Dark.png`) are applied the same way. Only if `awww` is missing or fails are the other tools tried: `swww`, Noctalia, `hyprpaper`, `swaybg`. To use your own command, set `"wallpaperCmd": "your-command {}"` (`{}` is the image path) in `~/.config/macbar/settings.json`. Animated (video) wallpapers need `mpvpaper` and `ffmpeg`. The Liquid Glass refracts your wallpaper, so the shell also needs its file path. It looks, in order, at: the `wallpaperPath` override in `settings.json`, Noctalia's `settings.toml`, `awww`/`swww query`, `hyprctl hyprpaper listactive`, and `~/.config/hypr/hyprpaper.conf`. If yours isn't detected (swaybg, wpaperd, a custom script), either pick a wallpaper in the built-in picker (it remembers the path), or set `"wallpaperPath": "/path/to/image.png"` in `~/.config/macdock/settings.json`. The picker reads `~/Pictures/Wallpapers` by default (`wallpaperDir`). ## Where things are stored | Path | Content | |---|---| | `~/.config/macbar/settings.json` | Menu bar settings | | `~/.config/macdock/settings.json`, `pinned.json` | Dock settings and pinned apps | | `~/.config/macdock/liquidglass.frag.qsb` | Compiled shader cache | | `~/.config/macwidgets/settings.json` | Desktop widgets, their placement and the widget size | | `~/.config/macwidgets/images/` | Pictures used by Image widgets | | `~/.local/share/macshell/` | Installer state, `macshell-update`, backups | | `~/.cache/macbar/` | Clipboard history helper files (images, timestamps) | | `~/Pictures/Screenshots` | Default screenshot folder | Clipboard history is kept on disk (cliphist's database plus `~/.cache/macbar/clip`). Turn it off with `clipHistory: false` in `~/.config/macbar/settings.json` if you don't want that. ## Fresh Arch install: recommended route 1. `sudo pacman -Syu`, then reboot if the kernel was updated. 2. Install Hyprland **0.55 or newer** and make sure you have a `hyprland.lua` (`hyprctl version` shows the version). 3. `git clone https://github.com/0-ss/MacShell && cd MacShell && bash install.sh` and answer yes. It installs every dependency (on Arch it can build `yay` for `awww` / `mpvpaper`), starts the Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, power-profile and audio services, adds the autostart to `hyprland.lua`, and creates `~/.config/macshell/env`. 4. Log out and back in (or run `sh ~/.local/bin/macshell-start`), then run `bash install.sh --doctor` if anything looks wrong. On older hardware add `--low-power`. **Environment variables** (`QS_ICON_THEME`, `QT_QPA_PLATFORM`, `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, ...): `macshell-start` sets sensible ones before it starts the shell, so it works whether it was started by Hyprland, a terminal or a keybind. Your own go in `~/.config/macshell/env` (the installer creates it with commented examples, including `QSG_RHI_BACKEND=opengl`, `QSG_RENDER_LOOP=basic` and `QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software` for old graphics). **Wallpaper after a reboot:** `awww` forgets its image at every shutdown. MacShell remembers the wallpaper you picked in the picker and puts it back at login (and `macshell-start` runs `awww restore` first). Pick a wallpaper once after updating and it stays. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Check | |---|---| | Glass looks flat / "Normal Blur" | `qsb` missing (install `qt6-shadertools`) — the log shows `[macbar-glass] state: failed`. Or ship a prebuilt `liquidglass.frag.qsb` next to `liquidglass.frag`; it is used as a fallback. | | Glass shows no wallpaper | Wallpaper not detected: see [Wallpaper](#wallpaper). | | Changing the wallpaper only changes the widgets and menus | `awww` is not installed or its daemon can't start. Install it, or set `wallpaperCmd` (see [Wallpaper](#wallpaper)); the log shows `[wallpaper] error:`. | | Blank app icons | No Qt icon theme: `macshell-start` picks your GTK theme or Papirus / WhiteSur / Tela / Adwaita if installed. Otherwise install one (`sudo pacman -S papirus-icon-theme`) or set `QS_ICON_THEME` in `~/.config/macshell/env`. | | Wallpaper is gone after a reboot | See [Fresh Arch install](#fresh-arch-install-recommended-route). Check `awww` is installed (`bash install.sh --doctor`) and pick the wallpaper once in the picker. | | Slow or choppy on an old laptop | `bash install.sh --low-power`, and try `QSG_RHI_BACKEND=opengl` in `~/.config/macshell/env`. | | No notifications | Another daemon owns the D-Bus name. Disable it and restart the shell. | | Window menu actions, Alt+Tab focus, paste-after-pick, Log Out or the floating Settings window do nothing | Not on a Lua-config Hyprland 0.55+: run `hyprctl dispatch 'hl.dsp.no_op()'`. | | No window previews / glass behind windows | Quickshell built without Hyprland Toplevel Export, or Settings → Dock Behavior → *Live window capture* is off. | | Bluetooth shows nothing / won't power on | `systemctl status bluetooth` must be active (`sudo systemctl enable --now bluetooth`), `bluetoothctl show` must list a controller, and `rfkill list bluetooth` must not say *Soft blocked: yes* (the switch in Control Center un-blocks it). Pairing a new device: put it in pairing mode, open Control Center → Bluetooth (it scans for 10 s) and click it. | | MacShell does not start with Hyprland | Hyprland 0.55+ with `hyprland.lua` ignores `hyprland.conf`: the autostart must be in the Lua file (`bash install.sh` puts it there). Test it by hand with `sh ~/.local/bin/macshell-start`. | | Log | `qs log` (see `qs --help` for selecting the config). | ## Known issues **Shell crash with `wl_display#1: error 0: invalid object NNN`** when many windows open/close quickly (a game launching, spamming terminals) while live window capture runs. A window closes while a capture frame for it is still pending; Hyprland does not answer that frame, the shell then destroys it, and the compositor drops the Wayland connection. Mitigations: - Settings → Menu Bar → turn **Real-time glass** off (far fewer captures; the biggest win). - Settings → Dock Behavior → turn **Live window capture** off. - The shell already pauses glass captures while windows open/close. - Auto-restart: the autostart the installer adds (`macshell-start`) already restarts the shell after a crash. **Glitchy window capture** (previews or glass showing a wrong or stale frame): turn off Settings → Dock Behavior → **Live window capture**. Reproduced on Hyprland 0.56.2 / Quickshell 0.3.2. ## Credits Created by [Rickky](https://github.com/0-ss) (owner), with [vSuol](https://github.com/vsoultann) (collaborator). Emoji data from [GitHub gemoji](https://github.com/github/gemoji) (MIT).

MacShell

A macOS Tahoe–style menu bar + Dock for Hyprland, built on Quickshell,
with a real-time Liquid Glass refraction shader, and a lock screen, MacLock.


Quick showcase (OLD)

Screenshots · Requirements · Install · Updating · Hyprland config · MacLock · Troubleshooting

--- A macOS Tahoe–style **menu bar + Dock** for Hyprland, built on [Quickshell](https://quickshell.org), with a real-time "Liquid Glass" refraction shader, window previews, Spotlight, clipboard/emoji picker, notifications, Control Center, screenshots, screen recording, desktop widgets (weather, calendar, clock, music player), a wallpaper picker, an Alt+Tab switcher and a full lock screen, all in one Quickshell process. The repository also ships **MacLock**, a matching Liquid Glass lock screen. It is a separate Quickshell config on purpose: it runs as its own process, so a shell crash can never take the lock with it. Best icon pack for the shell: https://github.com/Scrimas/MacOS-Like > **Heads up:** this targets **Hyprland 0.55+ with a Lua config** (`hyprland.lua`) and a recent **Quickshell (0.3.x)**. > See [Requirements](#requirements) and [Known issues](#known-issues).

**The whole desktop:** widgets, the menu bar on top and the Dock at the bottom.

**The Dock,** with Liquid Glass.

**Control Center**

Lock screen
Lock screen media player

```
MacShell/               (this repository)
├── install.sh          installer / updater
├── README.md
├── MacShell/           the shell      ->  ~/.config/quickshell/MacShell
└── MacLock/            the lock screen ->  ~/.config/quickshell/MacLock
```

The two are installed as **separate** Quickshell configs (neither lives inside the other).

**MacShell**

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `shell.qml` | Entry point. Shared hub: window geometry, wallpaper lookup, capture gating. |
| `MacBar.qml` | Menu bar, Control Center, Spotlight, notifications, switcher, screenshots, wallpaper picker. |
| `MacDock.qml` | Dock, window previews, and the Settings window. |
| `ClockApp.qml` | The Clock app window (opened from the menu bar clock). |
| `MacWidgets.qml` | Desktop widgets layer (data, placement, editing). |
| `WidgetVisual.qml` | Draws one widget; shared by the desktop layer and the Liquid Glass backdrop, so menus refract the widgets too. |
| `WeatherWidget.qml`, `WeatherIcon.qml`, `WeatherHourCol.qml`, `CalendarWidget.qml`, `ClockWidget.qml`, `PlayerWidget.qml`, `PlayerArt.qml`, `PlayerBtn.qml`, `PlayerGlyph.qml`, `ImageWidget.qml`, `MarqueeText.qml` | The widgets and their helpers (`ImageWidget.qml` shows a picture of your choice). |
| `SPopUp.qml`, `Dissolve.qml`, `MorphText.qml`, `MorphGlyph.qml`, `WGlyph.qml`, `ClockGlyph.qml`, `Wheel.qml` | Shared UI pieces and effects. |
| `liquidglass.frag` (+ `contourglow`, `tintcard`, `dust`, `burn`, `fade`) | Shaders. Prebuilt `.frag.qsb` files ship next to them; `liquidglass.frag` is recompiled with `qsb` on first run. |
| `EmojiData.js` | Emoji fallback data for Spotlight (from [gemoji](https://github.com/github/gemoji), MIT). |
| `macshell-update` | Update tool (installed to `~/.local/bin`, see [Updating](#updating)). The installer also writes `macshell-start`, the script the Hyprland autostart runs. |
| `apple-logo-black.svg`, `apple-logo-white.svg` | Menu bar logo. |
| `assets/` | Icons and the credits pictures. |

**MacLock**

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `shell.qml` | Entry point: session lock, IPC (`lockscreen`), preview mode. |
| `LockScreen.qml` | The lock screen UI and PAM password check. |
| `lock-via-ipc.sh` | Helper for your keybind: starts MacLock if needed, then locks. |
| `Glass.qml`, `Glyph.qml`, `MorphGlyph.qml`, `MorphText.qml`, `ClockGlyph.qml`, `ContourGlow.qml` and the `*.frag` / `*.qsb` shaders | Visuals. |
| `hyprland.lua` | Snippet with the keybind (copy it into your config). |

and more files...

| What | Why |
|---|---|
| **Hyprland ≥ 0.55, running a Lua config** (`~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`) | Window actions, the Alt+Tab focus, "paste after picking", Log Out and the floating Settings window use Lua dispatches (`hyprctl dispatch 'hl.dsp…'`, `hyprctl eval`). On older versions or a `.conf` session these actions fail; the bar, Dock, glass and previews still work. Quick test: `hyprctl dispatch 'hl.dsp.no_op()'` must not error. |
| **Quickshell ≥ 0.3.0** (0.3.2 recommended) | Needs the Hyprland module (`HyprlandToplevel`, `lastIpcObject`, Lua-config support), `ScreencopyView`, `IpcHandler`, and the UPower / Pipewire / Mpris / SystemTray / Notifications services. |
| Quickshell built with **Wayland**, **Hyprland**, **Screencopy → Hyprland Toplevel Export**, **Pipewire**, **UPower**, **Mpris**, **System Tray** | Distro packages normally enable all of these. Check the build info that `qs` prints in its logs. |
| **Qt 6.5+** with `qt6-declarative`, `qt6-wayland`, **`qt6-shadertools`** (provides `qsb`) | `QtQuick.Effects` (MultiEffect) needs 6.5+. `qsb` compiles `liquidglass.frag` on first run. Without it (and without a prebuilt `liquidglass.frag.qsb`) the glass falls back to "Normal Blur". |
| `qt6-svg` (recommended) | SVG app icons. |
| `hyprctl`, `sh`, `xdg-open` | Core. |
| An **icon theme** (Papirus, Adwaita, …) set for Qt apps | App icons in the Dock and Spotlight come from the system theme. If icons are blank, set one with `qt6ct` or `QS_ICON_THEME`. |
| `curl`, `tar` | Used by the installer and the updater, and by the Weather widget. |
| Font **Inter** (default) | Falls back to the system font; "Noto Sans" / "System" can be chosen in Settings. |

This shell **replaces** your bar, dock and notification daemon. Stop anything that overlaps:

- Other bars/shells (waybar, hyprpanel, ags, Noctalia, Caelestia, …) and docks (nwg-dock, …).
- Notification daemons (`dunst`, `mako`, `swaync`): the bar owns `org.freedesktop.Notifications`.
  `systemctl --user disable --now dunst` (or `mako` / `swaync`).

1. Install the requirements above. On Arch, for example:
   ```sh
    sudo pacman -Syu
    
    sudo pacman -S --needed \
      hyprland quickshell hyprlock awww \
      qt6-base qt6-declarative qt6-wayland qt6-shadertools qt6-svg \
      grim slurp wl-clipboard wf-recorder cliphist \
      libnotify brightnessctl \
      networkmanager bluez bluez-utils \
      inotify-tools \
      inter-font noto-fonts noto-fonts-emoji \
      xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland \
      xdg-utils polkit \
      pipewire wireplumber pipewire-pulse \
      kitty
   ```
   Other distros: install the equivalents. Fedora has a Quickshell COPR; Nix has `pkgs.quickshell`.
   You can skip this: the installer checks every requirement (tools, Qt libraries, fonts, icon theme, portals,
   `hyprlock`, the optional helpers such as `awww`, `zenity`, `slurp`, `ffmpeg`) and installs the missing ones for you
   with pacman, dnf or apt, after asking once (`-y` skips the question). Packages that are not in the main
   repositories, such as `quickshell` or `awww`, come from the AUR (`yay` / `paru`; on Arch the installer can build
   `yay` for you) or the Fedora COPR. It also enables the `bluetooth` service, which Bluetooth needs.
   `bash install.sh --deps-only` does just this step.
   Hyprland 0.55+ with a Lua config may need a newer package than your distro ships, so check `hyprctl version`.
   Debian/Ubuntu have no `quickshell` / `hyprland` packages: build those from source.
2. Run the installer, either from a clone:
   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/0-ss/MacShell
   cd MacShell
   bash install.sh
   ```
   or in one line:
   ```sh
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0-ss/MacShell/main/install.sh | bash
   ```
   It installs **MacShell** to `~/.config/quickshell/MacShell` and **MacLock** to `~/.config/quickshell/MacLock`,
   and adds the autostart to your Hyprland config: a block in `hyprland.lua` (Hyprland 0.55+), or an `exec-once`
   line in `hyprland.conf` when there is no Lua config. The block runs `~/.local/bin/macshell-start`, which waits for
   the compositor, never starts a second copy and restarts the shell if it crashes. Remove the block between the
   `MacShell (added by install.sh)` markers to undo it. Your settings are never touched, and the previous
   install is backed up first (last 3 kept in `~/.local/share/macshell/backups/`).

   When run from a clone, the installer first checks GitHub: if the repository has a newer version (and your clone has
   no uncommitted changes) it downloads and installs that one automatically.

   Don't reach the install folders through a symlink; Quickshell ≥ 0.3 derives its state folders from the link path.
3. Try it:
   ```sh
   qs -c MacShell
   ```
   On first run with the Liquid Glass style, `liquidglass.frag` is compiled with `qsb` and cached in
   `~/.config/macdock/liquidglass.frag.qsb`. Watch for `[macbar-glass] state: ready` in the log.
4. Add the Hyprland config below, then autostart it.

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `-y`, `--yes` | Don't ask questions (answer yes). |
| `--no-deps` | Skip the dependency check and package installation. |
| `--deps-only` | Only check / install dependencies (and enable the services below), then stop. |
| `--doctor` | Check the whole setup (environment, services, wallpaper, shaders, Hyprland, GPU) and explain each problem. |
| `--low-power` | Settings for older computers: no live window capture, no magnification, plain blur, no real-time glass. |
| `--no-services` | Don't enable system services (bluetooth, NetworkManager, power-profiles-daemon, PipeWire). |
| `--no-autostart` | Don't touch the Hyprland config. |
| `--no-rules` | Don't add the Liquid Glass layer rules to the Hyprland config. |
| `--channel release\|main` | `release` (default): latest release, or the newest commit if there are none. `main`: always the newest commit. |
| `--no-lock` | Install MacShell only, without MacLock. |
| `--check` | Only check for a newer version (exit 0 = up to date, 10 = update available). |
| `--local` | Install the local clone as it is, don't look for a newer version on GitHub. |
| `--auto-update` / `--no-auto-update` | Set up / remove a daily systemd user timer that installs updates by itself. |
| `--ref REF` | Install a specific tag or commit. |
| `--from-dir DIR` | Install from a local folder instead of downloading. |
| `--uninstall` | Remove MacShell and MacLock (settings are kept). |

Environment: `MACSHELL_REPO`, `MACSHELL_BRANCH`, `MACSHELL_CHANNEL`, `MACSHELL_DEST`, `MACLOCK_DEST`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

The Best way to make sure you have the latest update Is to delete the MacShell folder in /home (IF needed) and run this again :

   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/0-ss/MacShell
   cd MacShell
   bash install.sh
   ```
or you can use this method :

Run the installer (`./install.sh` in your clone, or `macshell-install` from anywhere). It shows a menu:

```
MacShell (installed: a1b2c3d4e5f6)

  1) Install shell
  2) Check for updates
  3) Uninstall shell
  4) Bind help
  q) Quit
```

- **Install shell** installs MacShell and MacLock (or reinstalls them).
- **Check for updates** compares your version with GitHub and, if there is a newer one, asks whether to install it (y/n).
- **Uninstall shell** removes MacShell and MacLock (your settings are kept).
- **Bind help** opens the Hyprland keybind section of this README in your browser.

The other tools are still available as options: `--doctor`, `--low-power`, `--deps-only` (see `--help`).

An update also installs the dependencies the new version needs, updates MacShell and MacLock together, saves the old
install first, and never touches your settings. The command-line tool is still there for scripts and the daily timer:

```sh
macshell-update check       # is there a newer version?
macshell-update log         # what changed since the installed version
macshell-update update      # download and install it (MacShell and MacLock), including new dependencies
macshell-update rollback    # go back to the previous install (MacShell and MacLock)
macshell-update channel main   # follow the newest commit instead of releases (or: release)
macshell-update status
```

`macshell-update update` runs the *new* version's installer too, so new files, new dependencies and a new start script
come along. It keeps the last 3 installs, and does one update at a time. Dependencies are installed only when `sudo` works without a password (an unattended timer
cannot type one); otherwise you get a notice listing what to install with `bash install.sh --deps-only`.

The shell also checks by itself and tells you. `bash install.sh --check` does the same check from a clone, and
`bash install.sh --auto-update` installs a daily timer (`systemctl --user list-timers macshell-update.timer`) so updates
install without you doing anything. MacShell reloads itself after an update; MacLock picks up the new files the next
time it locks.

```lua
-- autostart (remove other bars / docks / notification daemons first).
-- install.sh adds this for you; macshell-start waits for the compositor and restarts the shell if it crashes.
hl.on("hyprland.start", function()
    hl.exec_cmd("sh ~/.local/bin/macshell-start")
end)

-- layer rules: blur for the glass surfaces
hl.layer_rule({ name = "macdock",  match = { namespace = "macdock"  }, blur = true, ignore_alpha = 0.2,  no_anim = true })
hl.layer_rule({ name = "macspot",  match = { namespace = "macspot"  }, blur = true, ignore_alpha = 0.05, no_anim = true })
hl.layer_rule({ name = "macbarbg", match = { namespace = "macbarbg" }, blur = true, ignore_alpha = 0.05, no_anim = true })
hl.layer_rule({ name = "macshot",  match = { namespace = "macshot"  }, no_anim = true })   -- optional: no fade on the screenshot picker

-- The Settings window floats and centres itself when it opens, so it needs no window rule.

-- keybinds (the name after -c is the config folder name, case-sensitive)
local qs = "qs -c MacShell ipc call "

hl.bind("SUPER + V",          hl.dsp.exec_cmd(qs .. "spotlight clipboard"))
hl.bind("SUPER + period",     hl.dsp.exec_cmd(qs .. "spotlight emoji"))
hl.bind("SUPER + Space",      hl.dsp.exec_cmd(qs .. "spotlight toggle"))
hl.bind("ALT + TAB",          hl.dsp.exec_cmd(qs .. "switcher next"))
hl.bind("CTRL + ALT + W",     hl.dsp.exec_cmd(qs .. "wallpapers toggle"))
hl.bind("PRINT",              hl.dsp.exec_cmd(qs .. "screenshot region"))

-- MacLock (lock screen)
hl.bind("SUPER + L",          hl.dsp.exec_cmd("sh ~/.config/quickshell/MacLock/lock-via-ipc.sh"))
```

Change `SUPER + L` if that key is already used. On a classic `hyprland.conf` the same bind is
`bind = SUPER, L, exec, sh ~/.config/quickshell/MacLock/lock-via-ipc.sh`.

Also make sure **blur is enabled** in your Hyprland `decoration` settings, or the "Normal Blur" style won't blur.

`qs -c MacShell ipc call <target> <function>`

| Target | Functions |
|---|---|
| `spotlight` | `toggle`, `clipboard`, `emoji`, `apps` |
| `screenshot` | `region`, `screen`, `window` |
| `wallpapers` | `toggle`, `open`, `close` |
| `switcher` | `next`, `prev`, `commit`, `cancel` |
| `settings` | `open` (works even if both the bar and the Dock are disabled) |
| `widgets` | `refresh` (re-fetch the weather), `edit true\|false` (move / remove desktop widgets) |
| `glass` | `captures true\|false` (window previews on/off, same as Settings → Dock Behavior → *Live window capture*) |

A macOS-style lock screen using the same Liquid Glass look (see the [screenshots](#maclock-1) above). Each lock runs in
its own process (a Wayland session lock is used once), and `lock-via-ipc.sh` starts a fresh one for every lock, so the
keybind above is all you need.

```sh
sh ~/.config/quickshell/MacLock/lock-via-ipc.sh        # lock now (what the keybind runs)
qs -c MacLock ipc call lockscreen lock                 # same, if an IPC-ready MacLock is already running
qs -c MacLock                                          # lock immediately, one-shot (e.g. from hypridle)
MACLOCK_PREVIEW=1 qs -c MacLock                        # preview the design as a window, no real lock
```

Passwords are checked with PAM (`/etc/pam.d/hyprlock`). To lock on idle or before sleep with `hypridle`, set
`lock_cmd = sh ~/.config/quickshell/MacLock/lock-via-ipc.sh`.

Settings → Desktop & Dock → Icon Tint re-colours every Dock icon with one colour (pick a swatch or type a hex
colour) and works with any icon pack: each icon is desaturated and colourised with your colour, with a small
brightness lift so light colours (green, yellow...) stay vivid and black stays dark. **Strength** keeps some of the
original colours. It needs no shader build and no extra packages.

Settings → General → Desktop Widgets. Weather, Calendar, Clock, Player and **Image** widgets, each in Small, Medium
and Large. **Widget size** scales every widget and the grid together (60 % to 150 %); widgets snap back onto the
grid when you let go of the slider.

An Image widget shows a picture you choose: press **+ S / M / L** on the Image row and pick a file (needs `zenity`,
`kdialog` or `yad`). The picture is copied to `~/.config/macwidgets/images`, so it keeps working if the original
moves. To change it later use **Edit on Desktop** and press **Choose Image…** on the widget.

Changing the wallpaper from Settings, the wallpaper picker (Ctrl+Alt+W) or `ipc call wallpapers` sets the real desktop
wallpaper with **`awww`** (its daemon is started automatically if needed), and the widgets, menus and Liquid Glass follow.
Light/Dark wallpaper pairs (`name-Light.png` / `name-Dark.png`) are applied the same way. Only if `awww` is missing or
fails are the other tools tried: `swww`, Noctalia, `hyprpaper`, `swaybg`. To use your own command, set
`"wallpaperCmd": "your-command {}"` (`{}` is the image path) in `~/.config/macbar/settings.json`. Animated (video)
wallpapers need `mpvpaper` and `ffmpeg`.

The Liquid Glass refracts your wallpaper, so the shell also needs its file path. It looks, in order, at: the
`wallpaperPath` override in `settings.json`, Noctalia's `settings.toml`, `awww`/`swww query`,
`hyprctl hyprpaper listactive`, and `~/.config/hypr/hyprpaper.conf`. If yours isn't detected (swaybg, wpaperd, a custom
script), either pick a wallpaper in the built-in picker (it remembers the path), or set
`"wallpaperPath": "/path/to/image.png"` in `~/.config/macdock/settings.json`. The picker reads `~/Pictures/Wallpapers`
by default (`wallpaperDir`).

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `~/.config/macbar/settings.json` | Menu bar settings |
| `~/.config/macdock/settings.json`, `pinned.json` | Dock settings and pinned apps |
| `~/.config/macdock/liquidglass.frag.qsb` | Compiled shader cache |
| `~/.config/macwidgets/settings.json` | Desktop widgets, their placement and the widget size |
| `~/.config/macwidgets/images/` | Pictures used by Image widgets |
| `~/.local/share/macshell/` | Installer state, `macshell-update`, backups |
| `~/.cache/macbar/` | Clipboard history helper files (images, timestamps) |
| `~/Pictures/Screenshots` | Default screenshot folder |

Clipboard history is kept on disk (cliphist's database plus `~/.cache/macbar/clip`). Turn it off with `clipHistory: false`
in `~/.config/macbar/settings.json` if you don't want that.

1. `sudo pacman -Syu`, then reboot if the kernel was updated.
2. Install Hyprland **0.55 or newer** and make sure you have a `hyprland.lua` (`hyprctl version` shows the version).
3. `git clone https://github.com/0-ss/MacShell && cd MacShell && bash install.sh` and answer yes. It installs every
   dependency (on Arch it can build `yay` for `awww` / `mpvpaper`), starts the Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, power-profile and
   audio services, adds the autostart to `hyprland.lua`, and creates `~/.config/macshell/env`.
4. Log out and back in (or run `sh ~/.local/bin/macshell-start`), then run `bash install.sh --doctor` if anything
   looks wrong. On older hardware add `--low-power`.

**Environment variables** (`QS_ICON_THEME`, `QT_QPA_PLATFORM`, `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, ...): `macshell-start` sets
sensible ones before it starts the shell, so it works whether it was started by Hyprland, a terminal or a keybind.
Your own go in `~/.config/macshell/env` (the installer creates it with commented examples, including
`QSG_RHI_BACKEND=opengl`, `QSG_RENDER_LOOP=basic` and `QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software` for old graphics).

**Wallpaper after a reboot:** `awww` forgets its image at every shutdown. MacShell remembers the wallpaper you picked
in the picker and puts it back at login (and `macshell-start` runs `awww restore` first). Pick a wallpaper once after
updating and it stays.

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| Glass looks flat / "Normal Blur" | `qsb` missing (install `qt6-shadertools`) — the log shows `[macbar-glass] state: failed`. Or ship a prebuilt `liquidglass.frag.qsb` next to `liquidglass.frag`; it is used as a fallback. |
| Glass shows no wallpaper | Wallpaper not detected: see [Wallpaper](#wallpaper). |
| Changing the wallpaper only changes the widgets and menus | `awww` is not installed or its daemon can't start. Install it, or set `wallpaperCmd` (see [Wallpaper](#wallpaper)); the log shows `[wallpaper] error:`. |
| Blank app icons | No Qt icon theme: `macshell-start` picks your GTK theme or Papirus / WhiteSur / Tela / Adwaita if installed. Otherwise install one (`sudo pacman -S papirus-icon-theme`) or set `QS_ICON_THEME` in `~/.config/macshell/env`. |
| Wallpaper is gone after a reboot | See [Fresh Arch install](#fresh-arch-install-recommended-route). Check `awww` is installed (`bash install.sh --doctor`) and pick the wallpaper once in the picker. |
| Slow or choppy on an old laptop | `bash install.sh --low-power`, and try `QSG_RHI_BACKEND=opengl` in `~/.config/macshell/env`. |
| No notifications | Another daemon owns the D-Bus name. Disable it and restart the shell. |
| Window menu actions, Alt+Tab focus, paste-after-pick, Log Out or the floating Settings window do nothing | Not on a Lua-config Hyprland 0.55+: run `hyprctl dispatch 'hl.dsp.no_op()'`. |
| No window previews / glass behind windows | Quickshell built without Hyprland Toplevel Export, or Settings → Dock Behavior → *Live window capture* is off. |
| Bluetooth shows nothing / won't power on | `systemctl status bluetooth` must be active (`sudo systemctl enable --now bluetooth`), `bluetoothctl show` must list a controller, and `rfkill list bluetooth` must not say *Soft blocked: yes* (the switch in Control Center un-blocks it). Pairing a new device: put it in pairing mode, open Control Center → Bluetooth (it scans for 10 s) and click it. |
| MacShell does not start with Hyprland | Hyprland 0.55+ with `hyprland.lua` ignores `hyprland.conf`: the autostart must be in the Lua file (`bash install.sh` puts it there). Test it by hand with `sh ~/.local/bin/macshell-start`. |
| Log | `qs log` (see `qs --help` for selecting the config). |

**Shell crash with `wl_display#1: error 0: invalid object NNN`** when many windows open/close quickly (a game launching,
spamming terminals) while live window capture runs. A window closes while a capture frame for it is still pending; Hyprland
does not answer that frame, the shell then destroys it, and the compositor drops the Wayland connection. Mitigations:

- Settings → Menu Bar → turn **Real-time glass** off (far fewer captures; the biggest win).
- Settings → Dock Behavior → turn **Live window capture** off.
- The shell already pauses glass captures while windows open/close.
- Auto-restart: the autostart the installer adds (`macshell-start`) already restarts the shell after a crash.

**Glitchy window capture** (previews or glass showing a wrong or stale frame): turn off Settings → Dock Behavior →
**Live window capture**.

Reproduced on Hyprland 0.56.2 / Quickshell 0.3.2.
